items.title: Sidney "Jim Little" Brown Interview, 1960-05-27
items.q: I said, all right. And I just got my stuff together and went and joined with him. And after I played with him a while... I played with Papa from, uh, from, uh, 48 up until 59.

ctx.x: Well, you were still playing music right now while you worked there. While I was working for Bill. But otherwise, I mean, you were playing, you even played parades in those days too.

Oh, yeah. Well, that would be Sunday. Yeah. I mean, Sunday, that's the only time that they have parades, unless they have a day of funeral, you see. That was going to be a couple hours. You never put the music down? No, not completely, no. No. It went on like that and depression come on. It didn't pay the fool around with music. There was nothing to it. So, I almost put the bass in the corner and didn't play nothing. I'd get a job with a fellow to come at me and play on a Saturday night or a Sunday night. I'd be…
That's when Eddie Pearson had the band in the last couple years.
